title: FastAPI: REST, validation and errors
description: FastAPI routing and status codes, Pydantic v2 request validation and response models, 422 errors, and global exception handlers.
source: FastAPI documentation (handling errors, response model, parameters); Pydantic v2 documentation (validators, configuration, migration guide); Starlette documentation; MDN HTTP status codes
seriesDescription: Python and FastAPI interview topics in JEE-Advanced style: integer, assertion-reason, matrix match, fill-in-the-blanks, short Python/SQL code and multi-correct questions. Python only: nothing here mixes in Java.

questions.prompt: A FastAPI route takes body UserIn with name: str = Field(min_length=2), age: int = Field(ge=18) and password: str (required). A client posts {"name": "b", "age": 10}. How many entries are in the 422 response's detail list?
questions.explanation: Pydantic collects all errors rather than stopping at the first: name too short, age below 18, and password missing. One entry each.

questions.prompt: A FastAPI route takes a body model Order with items: list[Item], where Item has qty: int = Field(ge=1). A client posts {"items": [{"qty": 0}, {"qty": -1}, {"qty": 3}]}. How many entries are in the 422 response's detail list?
questions.explanation: Pydantic validates every list element and reports the two failures (items.0.qty and items.1.qty) with their locations; the valid third item adds nothing. Verified by running the route with TestClient.

questions.prompt: These routes are declared in this order: @app.get("/users/{uid}") def get(uid: int) and then @app.get("/users/me") def me(). What does GET /users/me return?

options.text: 422 with an int parsing error on uid.
options.why: Routes match in declaration order, so /users/{uid} captures 'me' and int validation fails.

options.text: 200 with the body "me".
options.why: This would only happen if the static route was declared first.

options.text: 404 because the paths are ambiguous.
options.why: FastAPI does not detect ambiguity; the first matching route wins.

options.text: 500 at startup because the two route patterns overlap and clash.
options.why: Declaring both is legal and causes no startup error.

questions.explanation: Declare fixed paths (/users/me) before parameterised ones (/users/{uid}). Verified by running the app.

questions.prompt: Write a Pydantic v2 model SignupIn with email: str and password: str (at least 8 characters, using Field). Add a field_validator on email that raises ValueError unless it contains '@' and otherwise returns it lower-cased.
questions.starter: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
questions.explanation: Pydantic v2 uses field_validator (v1 used validator). A ValueError in a validator becomes a 422 entry in FastAPI. Annotated types such as EmailStr (needs email-validator) are an alternative.

questions.prompt: A custom exception class OutOfStock(Exception) exists. Register a FastAPI handler so it produces HTTP 409 with JSON {"error": "out_of_stock"}.
questions.explanation: Handlers receive the request and the exception. For built-in errors you can override RequestValidationError or HTTPException handlers the same way.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: FastAPI answers 422 when a path parameter declared as int receives the text abc.
questions.reason: FastAPI is built on top of Starlette.

whys.a: Wrong: Starlette alone would not give 422; Pydantic validation does.
whys.b: Correct: both are true, but the 422 comes from Pydantic type validation of the declared annotation.
whys.d: Wrong: A is true; the detail has type int_parsing.

questions.explanation: FastAPI validates path, query, header and body values against type hints and returns 422 with a detail array on failure.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: A FastAPI route with response_model=UserOut will not leak a password field returned by the function.
questions.reason: response_model only affects the OpenAPI docs and never changes the response body.

whys.c: Correct: A is true because the return value is filtered and serialised through UserOut; R is false because filtering is real.

questions.explanation: response_model validates and filters the output, so extra fields are dropped. Keep separate input and output models so internal fields never reach the client.

questions.prompt: Given @app.post("/users", response_model=UserOut) def mk(u: UserIn): return u, where UserIn has name (stripped and title-cased by a validator), age and password, and UserOut has only name and age. A client posts {"name": " bo ", "age": 20, "password": "x"}. What comes back?

options.text: Status 200 with {"name": "Bo", "age": 20}.
options.why: The validator ran on input and the filter dropped password on output.

options.text: Status 201 with {"name": "bo", "age": 20, "password": "x"} echoed back to the client.
options.why: Default status is 200 and password is filtered out.

options.text: Status 422 because the returned object is not a UserOut.
options.why: FastAPI converts the returned object via the response model.

options.text: Status 200 with {"name": " bo ", "age": 20}.
options.why: The input validator already cleaned the name before the handler ran.

questions.explanation: Verified by running it. POST gives 200 unless status_code=201 is declared.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which of these are default FastAPI/Starlette behaviours?

options.text: A missing required query parameter gives 422.
options.why: The query parameter is validated and a missing value is a validation error.

options.text: An unknown URL gives 404.
options.why: No route matches, so Starlette returns Not Found.

options.text: A POST to a path that only has GET gives 405.
options.why: The path matches but the method does not, so Method Not Allowed.

options.text: raise HTTPException(404, "nope") gives JSON {"detail": "nope"}.
options.why: The default handler serialises detail as JSON.

options.text: An unhandled ValueError in the route gives 400.
options.why: Unhandled exceptions become a 500 Internal Server Error.

options.text: A validation error gives 400 with a plain text body.
options.why: FastAPI returns 422 with a JSON detail list.

questions.explanation: Verified by running the app. Customise with exception_handler for HTTPException, RequestValidationError or your own types.

questions.prompt: Write a Pydantic v2 model ProfileIn with a field nickname: str that rejects any request body containing fields it does not declare, so FastAPI answers 422 for them.

checks.label: configures extra as forbid through model_config

questions.explanation: Pydantic v2 uses model_config (v1 used an inner class Config). The error type is extra_forbidden. The value "ignore" is the default and "allow" stores the extras on the model.

questions.prompt: Match each Pydantic v1 API with its Pydantic v2 replacement.
questions.explanation: Pydantic v2 prefixes the instance and class API with model_ and moves configuration into model_config. The v1 names still exist as deprecated aliases but emit warnings, and pre-2.0 tutorials still use them.

questions.prompt: A client posts {"name": "Ann", "role": "admin"} to a route whose Pydantic v2 request model declares only name. With default settings, what happens to the unknown role field?

options.text: The request fails with 422 because role is not declared.
options.why: 422 for extras needs extra="forbid" on the model.

options.text: It is silently ignored and the request succeeds.
options.why: Correct: Pydantic v2 ignores extra input by default (extra="ignore").

options.text: The field is stored on the model instance as an extra attribute.
options.why: That is extra="allow"; it is not the default.

options.text: FastAPI answers 400 Bad Request listing the extra field.
options.why: FastAPI validation failures use 422, and extras are not failures by default.

questions.explanation: Strictness is opt-in: model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid"). Ignoring extras is also why passing request data straight into ORM objects invites mass assignment; copy fields explicitly.

questions.prompt: Write a FastAPI POST /users route named create that takes a body model UserIn, returns UserOut through response_model, answers status 201, and returns service.create(body).
questions.explanation: Set a Location header through a Response parameter if the client needs the new URL. Without status_code the default for POST is 200.

questions.prompt: Match each FastAPI handler parameter with where its value is read from.

left.text: user_id: int, when the path is /users/{user_id}
limit: int = 10, not part of the path

questions.explanation: FastAPI infers the source from the signature: names found in the path are path parameters, scalar types are query parameters, models are bodies. Header() converts underscores to hyphens.

questions.prompt: True or false: a parameter declared as x_token: str = Header() reads the request header X-Token (underscores converted to hyphens by default).

options.text: True
options.why: Correct: FastAPI converts the underscores, and HTTP header names are case-insensitive.

options.text: False
options.why: The conversion is on by default because underscores in header names are problematic for many proxies.

questions.explanation: Set convert_underscores=False only if you really need a header name that contains underscores.

questions.prompt: True or false: by default FastAPI answers 400 Bad Request when request validation fails.

options.text: True
options.why: Wrong: validation failures are not 400 in FastAPI.

options.text: False
options.why: Correct: the default is 422 Unprocessable Entity with a JSON detail list.

questions.explanation: Override the RequestValidationError handler if your API contract says 400. The detail entries carry loc, msg and type fields.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: A Pydantic field declared only as name: str accepts the empty string.
questions.reason: A bare str annotation requires a string value but puts no constraint on its length.

whys.a: Correct: "" is a valid str; use Field(min_length=1) to reject it.
whys.b: Wrong: R is the exact reason.

questions.explanation: Add Field(min_length=1) or a constrained type (Annotated[str, StringConstraints(min_length=1, strip_whitespace=True)]) to reject blank values.
